search_text returns releases where query is in headline or body (case-insensitive); preserves order

Ensure deterministic lifecycle and rendering without external dependencies
Provide a minimal yet complete runtime demo and concise automated tests
Requirement Analysis: We must implement a Python 3.10 domain package for custom press releases with a strict 10-file layout and a single pytest suite. Main.py remains a thin entrypoint exposing run_demo. Core modules define errors, types, template rendering with a literal sorted-field replacement loop, validation, a mutable PressRelease with state transitions, and search utilities. No datetime/time/random/uuid/pathlib/os/threading or clock abstractions are permitted. The constructor for PressRelease is non-validating; validations return booleans; invalid transitions raise domain-specific exceptions. Version history uses monotonically increasing integer numbers and captures rendered text on first publish. __init__.py re-exports only canonical names. Tests must be concise (3 cases), deterministic, import run_demo from Main, and confirm lifecycle, rendering, validation, and search behaviors. Maintain an acyclic import graph: errors -> types -> template -> validation -> press_release -> search -> __init__ -> Main -> tests.
Requirement Pool: Preserve protocol files and test command exactly (requirements.txt, Main.py, tests/test_main.py; python -m pytest -q)
Implement domain entities: errors, types (State, Contact, VersionEntry), Template, validators, PressRelease, search
Enforce lifecycle transitions with specified error semantics and deterministic version history
Implement run_demo demonstrating a non-interactive lifecycle up to PUBLISHED
Provide concise, deterministic tests covering demo, rendering, validation, transitions, tags, and search
Testing Constraints: Exactly one protocol-level test file: tests/test_main.py
No manual interaction; no network; no OS-specific behavior
Minimal, concise coverage of runtime wiring and core rules
Tests import run_demo only from Main; all other symbols from press_releases
UI / UX / Interaction Design draft: No GUI. Provide a minimal console-friendly run_demo that returns a dict with key domain objects and states; only print a concise line under __name__ guard. Tests are headless and avoid real IO, network, or OS interactions.
User Stories: As an editor, I can draft a press release with a headline, body, contact, and custom fields.
As an editor, I can validate and submit a draft for review, and publish it when ready.
As a content manager, I can render drafts using a template with placeholders.
As a marketer, I can tag releases and find them by tag or text search.
As a reviewer, I can rely on a versioned, deterministic publishing process.
